If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to hedge downside risk.  
For mid-horizon (8–15 days), if sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), apply a 0.5–1.0% upward bias if recent price is rising, or downward bias if falling.  
For late-horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive and price is trending up, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect sustained momentum.  
If sentiment is negative and price is trending down, subtract 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) in last 5 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing adjustment to forecast to reduce overfitting.
